lessons.notes_html:
This book is the Balochistan Textbook Board's Class 3 Mathematics book (English medium, based on the National Curriculum 2022-23). It has seven units: Whole Numbers, Number Operations, Fractions, Measurement of Length, Mass, Capacity and Temperature, Time, Geometry, and Data Handling and Probability, plus a Glossary at the end.

In these solved notes every lesson is summarised and every exercise is solved step by step. Where the book gives only reading, counting practice or a practical activity, that work is stated clearly so the pupil can do it.

Learning Outcomes

Students' Learning Outcomes (page 5): Count up to 9999 (4-digit numbers). Read and write up to 999 in numerals and in words. Recognise the place value of each digit in 4-digit numbers. Compare numbers using symbols and arrange numbers up to 9999 using appropriate language. Round numbers to the nearest tens, hundreds and thousands using different concrete and pictorial representations. Read and write Roman numbers up to 20. Recognise and differentiate between even and odd numbers.

We have already learned numbers up to 999. Before we start, let's quickly recap.

lessons.title: Counting Numbers up to 9999 (page 7)

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 3-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest 3-digit number has 9 in every place, which is 999, as stated in the lesson notes.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number?
mcqs.why: Adding 1 to the greatest 3-digit number gives 999 + 1 = 1000, which is the smallest 4-digit number.

mcqs.q: What is 999 + 1?
mcqs.why: Adding ones first: 9 + 1 = 10, carrying through gives 999 + 1 = 1000, the smallest 4-digit number.

mcqs.q: How do we read 1000 in words?
mcqs.why: The number 1000 is read as one thousand, because the 1 is in the thousands place.

mcqs.q: How is 336 written in words?
mcqs.why: 336 has 3 hundreds, 3 tens and 6 ones, so it is written as three hundred and thirty-six.

mcqs.q: How is 452 written in words?
mcqs.why: 452 has 4 hundreds, 5 tens and 2 ones, so it is written as four hundred and fifty-two.

mcqs.q: How is 999 written in words?
mcqs.why: 999 has 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 9 ones, so it is written as nine hundred and ninety-nine.

mcqs.q: How many digits are there in 1000?
mcqs.why: The number 1000 is made of the digits 1, 0, 0 and 0, which is 4 digits in total.

mcqs.q: What number comes just before 1000?
mcqs.why: Subtracting 1 gives the previous number: 1000 - 1 = 999, so 999 comes just before 1000.

mcqs.q: 999 is a number with how many digits?
mcqs.why: 999 is made of three digits, 9, 9 and 9, so it is a 3-digit number, the greatest one.

lessons.notes_html:
Now we will learn 4-digit numbers up to 9999. Look at the 3-digit numbers below: 336 = Three hundred and thirty-six; 452 = Four hundred and fifty-two; 999 = Nine hundred and ninety-nine. Add one: 999 + 1 = 1000. In the above, 1 more block added which completed 1000. Since 999 is the greatest 3-digit number, when we add 1 to the 3-digit number that is 999 + 1, we get the smallest 4-digit number that is 1,000. We read it as 'one thousand'.

Counting Numbers up to 9999 (page 7): 999 + 1 = ?

Step 1: 999 is the greatest 3-digit number.

Step 2: Add 1 to 999.

Step 3: 999 + 1 = 1000.

Step 4: 1000 is the smallest 4-digit number.

Step 5: We read 1000 as 'one thousand'.

Answer: 1000

mcqs.q: In the counting chart, the first row 1000 to 1009 starts with which number?
mcqs.why: The chart on page 8 starts counting at 1000, so the first row begins with the number 1000.

mcqs.q: The row 1000 to 1009 ends with which number?
mcqs.why: A row of ten starting at 1000 runs 1000, 1001, up to 1009, so the row ends with 1009.

mcqs.q: What number comes just after 1005 in the row 1000 to 1009?
mcqs.why: Counting forward adds 1 each time: 1005 + 1 = 1006, so the number after 1005 is 1006.

mcqs.q: In the row 1010 to 1019, what number comes just after 1014?
mcqs.why: Counting forward adds 1 each time: 1014 + 1 = 1015, so the number after 1014 is 1015.

mcqs.q: The row starting with 2020 ends with which number?
mcqs.why: A row of ten starting at 2020 runs up to 2020 + 9 = 2029, so the row ends with 2029.

mcqs.q: In the chart, the row 2030 to 2039 comes just after the row ending with which number?
mcqs.why: Rows follow in order, so the row 2030 to 2039 comes right after the row that ends with 2029.

mcqs.q: The last row of the chart is 9990 to 9999. What is the greatest number in it?
mcqs.why: The last row runs from 9990 up to 9999, so the greatest number in the row is 9999.

mcqs.q: What number comes just after 9995 in the row 9990 to 9999?
mcqs.why: Counting forward adds 1 each time: 9995 + 1 = 9996, so the number after 9995 is 9996.

mcqs.q: How many numbers are there in each row of the counting chart?
mcqs.why: Each row of the chart, such as 1000 to 1009, holds ten numbers counted one after another.

mcqs.q: What is the first number of the last row, 9990 to 9999?
mcqs.why: The last row is written as 9990 to 9999, so it starts with the number 9990.

lessons.title: Place value (pages 17 to 18)

mcqs.q: In 5432, which digit is in the thousands place?
mcqs.why: Reading from the left, 5432 has thousands 5, hundreds 4, tens 3 and ones 2, so the thousands digit is 5.

mcqs.q: In 5432, which digit is in the ones place?
mcqs.why: Reading from the left, 5432 has thousands 5, hundreds 4, tens 3 and ones 2, so the ones digit is 2.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of 4 in 4532?
mcqs.why: In 4532 the digit 4 is in the thousands place, so its place value is 4 thousands = 4000.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of 3 in 4532?
mcqs.why: In 4532 the digit 3 is in the tens place, so its place value is 3 tens = 30.

mcqs.q: In 3402, which digit is in the tens place?
mcqs.why: 3402 has thousands 3, hundreds 4, tens 0 and ones 2, so the digit in the tens place is 0.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of 7 in 5721?
mcqs.why: In 5721 the digit 7 is in the hundreds place, so its place value is 7 hundreds = 700.

mcqs.q: A number has 2 thousands, 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 6 ones. What is the number?
mcqs.why: Putting the digits in order thousands, hundreds, tens, ones gives 2, 3, 6, 6, which makes the number 2366.

mcqs.q: In 6450, which digit is in the hundreds place?
mcqs.why: 6450 has thousands 6, hundreds 4, tens 5 and ones 0, so the digit in the hundreds place is 4.

mcqs.q: In 5325, the digit 2 is in the tens place. What is its place value?
mcqs.why: The digit 2 in the tens place means 2 tens, and 2 x 10 = 20, so its place value is 20.

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 3-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest 3-digit number has 9 in every place, which is 999, before 1000 starts the 4-digit numbers.

lessons.notes_html:
We have already learnt about the place values of 3-digit numbers. We know that 99 is the greatest 2-digit number. 1 more than 99 is 100. 100 is the first 3-digit number. We can show it in place value as: 1 in the Hundreds place, 0 in the Tens place, 0 in the Ones place. We can show the number 111: 1 hundred, 1 ten and 1 one. We know that 999 is the largest (greatest) 3-digit number. If we add 1 more in 999, it becomes 1000. It is the first (smallest) 4-digit number. We can show the place of each digit as: 1 in the Thousands place, 0 in the Hundreds place, 0 in the Tens place, 0 in the Ones place.

Example (page 18): Identify the place of each digit of 5432. Solution: Thousands = 5, Hundreds = 4, Tens = 3, Ones = 2. Example (page 18, already completed in the book): 232 = Hundreds 2, Tens 3, Ones 2; 6450 = Thousands 6, Hundreds 4, Tens 5, Ones 0; 5634 = Thousands 5, Hundreds 6, Tens 3, Ones 4; 7021 = Thousands 7, Hundreds 0, Tens 2, Ones 1. Example (page 18): Write the place value of 4532: 2 ones = 2; 3 tens = 30; 5 hundreds = 500; 4 thousands = 4000.

lessons.title: Comparing numbers up to 9999 using symbols (pages 21 to 23)

mcqs.q: What does the symbol < mean?
mcqs.why: The symbol < means less than; it is used to show that the first number is smaller than the second number.

mcqs.q: What does the symbol > mean?
mcqs.why: The symbol > means greater than; it is used to show that the first number is bigger than the second number.

mcqs.q: Compare 3745 and 4414. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: Compare the thousands digits: 3 and 4. Since 3 < 4, we get 3745 < 4414, as shown in the example.

mcqs.q: Compare 3364 and 3344. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: Thousands and hundreds are equal, then compare tens: 6 > 4, so 3364 > 3344, as shown in the example.

mcqs.q: Compare 999 and 1000. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: A number with more digits is always greater: 1000 has 4 digits and 999 has 3 digits, so 999 < 1000.

mcqs.q: Compare 5234 and 4234. Which number is greater?
mcqs.why: Both have the same digits count, so compare the leftmost digits: 5 > 4, which means 5234 is greater.

mcqs.q: In 3364 and 3344, thousands and hundreds are equal. Which place is compared next?
mcqs.why: After thousands and hundreds match, we compare the tens digits 6 and 4 next, and 6 > 4 decides the answer.

mcqs.q: Which symbol compares 2567 and 2567 correctly?
mcqs.why: Both numbers are exactly the same, 2567 = 2567, so the equal to symbol = is the correct symbol.

mcqs.q: Compare 4812 and 4912. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: Thousands are equal at 4, then compare hundreds: 8 < 9, so 4812 < 4912 by the left-to-right rule.

mcqs.q: Compare 7300 and 7200. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: Thousands are equal at 7, then compare hundreds: 3 > 2, so 7300 > 7200 by the left-to-right rule.

lessons.notes_html:
The comparison of four digit numbers can be done in the same way as we did for the 3-digit numbers. Key note: we use symbols to compare two numbers: < less than, > greater than, = equal to. Step I: If a number has more digits than other number, so it is always greater. Step II: If two numbers have the same number of digits, then the number with greater digit on the extreme left is greater.

Example (page 21): Compare 3745 and 4414

Step 1: Compare the thousands digits of 3745 and 4414.

Step 2: They are 3 and 4.

Step 3: As 3 < 4, 3745 is less than 4414.

Step 4: So we write 3745 < 4414.

Answer: 3745 < 4414

Example (pages 21 to 22): Compare 3364 and 3344

Step 1: Compare thousands digits: they are equal (3 = 3).

Step 2: Compare hundreds digits: they are equal (3 = 3).

Step 3: Compare tens digits: they are 6 and 4.

Step 4: As 6 > 4, 3364 is greater than 3344.

Step 5: So we write 3364 > 3344.

Answer: 3364 > 3344

lessons.title: Rounding Numbers (pages 24 to 26)

mcqs.q: When rounding, if the digit on the right is 5 or more, what do we do?
mcqs.why: The general rounding rule says: if the digit on the right is 5 or more, round up to the next value.

mcqs.q: Round off 17 to the nearest 10.
mcqs.why: The ones digit of 17 is 7, which is 5 or more, so round up: 17 is nearer to 20 than to 10, giving 20.

mcqs.q: Round off 342 to the nearest 100.
mcqs.why: The tens digit of 342 is 4, which is 4 or less, so round down: 342 is nearer to 300 than to 400, giving 300.

mcqs.q: Round off 26 to the nearest 10.
mcqs.why: The ones digit of 26 is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to the next ten: 26 rounds to 30.

mcqs.q: Round off 53 to the nearest 10.
mcqs.why: The ones digit of 53 is 3, which is 4 or less, so round down to the lower ten: 53 rounds to 50.

mcqs.q: Round off 269 to the nearest 100.
mcqs.why: The tens digit of 269 is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to the next hundred: 269 rounds to 300.

mcqs.q: Round off 5453 to the nearest 1000.
mcqs.why: The hundreds digit of 5453 is 4, which is less than 5, so replace the last three digits by 0: 5453 rounds to 5000.

mcqs.q: Round off 5744 to the nearest 1000.
mcqs.why: The hundreds digit of 5744 is 7, which is more than 5, so increase thousands by 1 and use zeros: 5744 rounds to 6000.

mcqs.q: Round off 4800 to the nearest 1000.
mcqs.why: The hundreds digit of 4800 is 8, which is 5 or more, so increase thousands by 1 and use zeros: 4800 rounds to 5000.

mcqs.q: What does rounding a number mean?
mcqs.why: Rounding means giving a number a nearby value, so the number becomes easier to use or easier to remember.

lessons.notes_html:
Rounding means giving a number a nearby value. People sometimes round the numbers to make numbers that are easier to use or easier to remember. General Rounding Rules: Finding the place where you are going to do rounding, then look at the digit on the right. If the digit is 5 or more, round up. If the digit is 4 or less, round down.

Rounding numbers to the nearest 10 (page 24): The round to the nearest 10 gives a number the value of tens it is closest to. When the ones digit is 5 or more, round up. When it is 4 or less, round down. We can use a number line to round off a number. Let's round off 17 to the nearest 10. It shows that 17 is nearest to 20 than to 10, so 17 is rounded up to 20.

Rounding numbers to the nearest 100 (pages 24 to 25): Similarly, we can round off to the nearest 100. Let's round off 342 to the nearest 100. It shows that 342 is nearest to 300 than to 400, so 342 is rounded down to 300.

Another Method of Rounding Off Numbers - Rounding Numbers to the Nearest 1000 (page 25): We will use two steps to round off to the nearest 1000. If the digit in the hundreds place is less than 5, then the ones, tens and hundreds place digits are replaced by '0'. If the digit in the hundreds place is 5 or greater than 5, then the ones, tens and hundreds place digits are replaced by '0' and the thousands place digit is increased by '1'. Let's round off 5453 to the nearest 1000. In 5453 the digit in the hundreds place is less than 5. Here, we replace 4, 5 and 3 by '0'. So, 5453 rounded off to the nearest 1000 is 5000. Let's round off 5744 to the nearest 1000. In 5744 the digit in the hundreds place is greater than 5. Here, we increase the thousands place digit by '1' and replace the tens, ones and hundreds place digits by '0'. So, 5744 rounded off to the nearest 1000 is 6000.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Roman Numbers up to 20 (pages 27 to 28)

mcqs.q: What is 4 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: A smaller symbol on the left is subtracted: 5 - 1 = 4, so V - I = IV is the Roman numeral for 4.

mcqs.q: What is 9 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: A smaller symbol on the left is subtracted: 10 - 1 = 9, so X - I = IX is the Roman numeral for 9.

mcqs.q: What is 5 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: The symbol V stands for the number 5 in Roman numerals, as shown in the list from 1 to 20.

mcqs.q: What is 7 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: A smaller symbol on the right is added: 5 + 1 + 1 = 7, so V + I + I = VII is the Roman numeral for 7.

mcqs.q: What is 12 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: The values are added together: 10 + 1 + 1 = 12, so X + I + I = XII is the Roman numeral for 12.

mcqs.q: What is 20 written in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: The symbol X can be repeated: 10 + 10 = 20, so X + X = XX is the Roman numeral for 20.

mcqs.q: What number does XIV stand for?
mcqs.why: In XIV, the I before V is subtracted and the rest added: 10 + (5 - 1) = 10 + 4 = 14, so XIV stands for 14.

mcqs.q: What number does XVIII stand for?
mcqs.why: In XVIII, all values are added: 10 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 18, so XVIII stands for the number 18.

mcqs.q: For which number is there no symbol in the Roman numeration system?
mcqs.why: The key note in the lesson states clearly that there is no symbol for 0 in the Roman numeration system.

mcqs.q: Which symbol can never be repeated in Roman numerals?
mcqs.why: The lesson rules state that the symbol V cannot be repeated, while I and X can repeat up to three times.

lessons.notes_html:
Roman numbers were used by ancient Romans in between 800 - 900 B.C. These are frequently used in daily life. We have seen the Roman numbers on the dials of clocks, watches and clock towers in big cities. Sometimes these numbers are also used in examination papers and books. Roman numbers from 1 to 20 are based on the symbols: I, V, X. Read Roman numbers given below: 1 = I (i), 2 = II (ii), 3 = III (iii), 4 = IV (iv), 5 = V (v), 6 = VI (vi), 7 = VII (vii), 8 = VIII (viii), 9 = IX (ix), 10 = X (x), 11 = XI (xi), 12 = XII (xii), 13 = XIII (xiii), 14 = XIV (xiv), 15 = XV (xv), 16 = XVI (xvi), 17 = XVII (xvii), 18 = XVIII (xviii), 19 = XIX (xix), 20 = XX (xx).

Some rules to write Roman numbers are: 1. I, X can be repeated up to three times, so formed as: 1 = I, 2 = I + I = II, 3 = I + I + I = III, 10 = X, 12 = 10 + 1 + 1 = XII, 20 = 10 + 10 = XX. 2. When a symbol of smaller value is placed on the left of a symbol of bigger value, we subtract their values to find the Roman numeral: 5 - 1 = 4 = V - I = IV, and 10 - 1 = 9 = X - I = IX. 3. When a symbol of smaller value is placed on the right we add their value to find the Roman numeral, so formed as: 5 + 1 = 6 = V + I = VI, 5 + 2 = 7 = V + I + I = VII. Key note: There is no symbol for '0' in Roman numeration system. The symbol I can be written to the left or right of symbol V and X. Symbol V cannot be repeated. NOTE - the book prints rule 2's second example as '9 - 1 = 10 = X - I = IX'; the correct subtraction is 10 - 1 = 9 = X - I = IX, and that is what is used here.

lessons.title: Even and Odd Numbers (pages 30 to 31)

mcqs.q: Even numbers end in which digits?
mcqs.why: The key note says even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, because their ones digit is one of these.

mcqs.q: Odd numbers end in which digits?
mcqs.why: The key note says odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, because their ones digit is one of these.

mcqs.q: Is 62 an even or an odd number?
mcqs.why: 62 ends in 2 and is divisible by 2, since 62 / 2 = 31 exactly, so 62 is an even number.

mcqs.q: Is 43 an even or an odd number?
mcqs.why: 43 ends in 3 and is not divisible by 2, since 43 / 2 leaves a remainder, so 43 is an odd number.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is even: 43, 83, 74, 39?
mcqs.why: Only 74 ends in 4, an even ones digit, and 74 / 2 = 37 exactly, so 74 is the even number here.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is odd: 54, 33, 66, 46?
mcqs.why: Only 33 ends in 3, an odd ones digit, and 33 is not divisible by 2, so 33 is the odd number here.

mcqs.q: What is the first even number between 5 and 13?
mcqs.why: Counting from 5: 6 is the first number ending in an even digit, and the even numbers here are 6, 8, 10, 12.

mcqs.q: Write E for even or O for odd: 366 is _____?
mcqs.why: 366 ends in 6 and is divisible by 2, since 366 / 2 = 183 exactly, so 366 is even and we write E.

mcqs.q: Write E for even or O for odd: 999 is _____?
mcqs.why: 999 ends in 9 and is not divisible by 2, since it leaves a remainder, so 999 is odd and we write O.

mcqs.q: Numbers which are divisible by 2 are called what?
mcqs.why: The lesson says the numbers which are divisible by 2 are called even numbers, with nothing left over.

lessons.notes_html:
Even Numbers (page 30): The objects or things that are even can be grouped in pairs. For example in the given figure, the objects show the even numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. So, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 are even numbers. Key note: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. The numbers in which the digit at ones place is 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 are called even numbers. Remember: The numbers which are divisible by 2 are called even numbers.

Odd Numbers (page 31): The objects or things that are odd cannot be grouped in pairs. For example, in the given figure the objects show the odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. So, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 are odd numbers. Key note: Odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9. Remember: The numbers which are not divisible by 2 are called odd numbers. lessons.title: Unit 1 Summary (page 35)

mcqs.q: Arranging numbers from smallest to greatest is called what?
mcqs.why: The summary states that arranging numbers in order from smallest to greatest is called ascending order.

mcqs.q: Arranging numbers from greatest to smallest is called what?
mcqs.why: The summary states that arranging numbers in order from greatest to smallest is called descending order.

mcqs.q: Roman numerals from 1 to 20 are based on which three symbols?
mcqs.why: The summary states that Roman numerals 1 to 20 are based on the three symbols I, V and X.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is even: 37, 42, 65, 79?
mcqs.why: Only 42 ends in 2, and all even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, so 42 is the even number.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is odd: 10, 32, 81, 86?
mcqs.why: Only 81 ends in 1, and all odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, so 81 is the odd number.

mcqs.q: What does rounding off a number mean?
mcqs.why: The summary states that rounding means giving a number a nearby value, to make it easier to use.

mcqs.q: Which symbols are used for comparing numbers?
mcqs.why: The summary lists comparing of numbers using the symbols <, > or =, for less than, greater than and equal to.

mcqs.q: In Unit 1, place value is identified for numbers up to how many digits?
mcqs.why: The summary lists identifying the place value of numbers up to 4 digits, from ones up to thousands.

mcqs.q: In Unit 1, numbers are written in words up to which number?
mcqs.why: The summary lists writing the numbers in words up to 999, such as nine hundred ninety nine for 999.

mcqs.q: Which vocabulary word means giving a number a nearby value?
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list includes Rounding Off, which the summary defines as giving a number a nearby value.

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Counting and reading the numbers up to 4 digits.
  • Writing the numbers in words up to 999.
  • Identifying the place value of numbers up to 4 digits.
  • Comparing of numbers using symbols <, > or =.
  • Arranging numbers in order from smallest to greatest is called ascending order.
  • Arranging numbers in order from greatest to smallest is called descending order.
  • Rounding off numbers nearest to 10, 100 and 1000.
  • Roman numerals 1 - 20 are based on three symbols: I, V, X.
  • All even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
  • All odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
  • Rounding means giving a number a nearby value.
  • Vocabulary: Count, Thousand, Arrange, Place Value, Roman, before, after, Rounding Off, between.
  • This closes Unit 1 (pages 5 to 35).

lessons.notes_html:
Learning Outcomes

Students' Learning Outcomes (page 36): Add and subtract numbers mentally and in written form (with and without regrouping) including 4-digit numbers with 1, 2, 3 and 4-digit numbers. Solve real-world word problems (including missing numbers and money) involving addition and subtraction. Estimate the answer to an addition and subtraction question (using various approaches). Count and write in multiple steps. Write out developed times tables for 6, 7, 8, and 9 and write multiplication sentences using concrete and pictorial representations. Reinforce through concrete and pictorial representations that the multiplication of any two numbers can be done in any order. Multiply mentally and in written form: 2-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers. Solve real-world word problems involving multiplication. Reinforce through concrete and pictorial representation that the division of any two numbers cannot be done in any order (Commutative). Divide mentally and in written form: 2-digit numbers by 1-digit number (with and without remainder), 3-digit numbers with 1-digit numbers (with and without remainder). Divide a number by 1 and itself. Solve real-world word problems involving division. Solve real-world word problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. Recognise and extend a given number pattern in increasing and decreasing order. Find the missing number or operation in a number sentence (e.g., 20 + W = 100).

We have already learnt addition of numbers up to 3 digits in class 2.

lessons.title: Real-World Word Problems  -  Addition (page 55)

mcqs.q: A train travelled 2360 km on the first day and 1235 km on the second day. How far did it travel in two days?
mcqs.why: Add the two distances: 2360 + 1235. Ones 0+5=5, tens 6+3=9, hundreds 3+2=5, thousands 2+1=3, giving 3595 km.

mcqs.q: In Malakand 1335 houses and in Waziristan 660 houses were damaged. How many houses were damaged in both cities?
mcqs.why: Add 1335 + 660: ones 5+0=5, tens 3+6=9, hundreds 3+6=9, thousands 1, giving 1995 houses damaged in both cities.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sold 2472 kg of rice in the first week and 2215 kg in the second week. How much rice did he sell in two weeks?
mcqs.why: Add 2472 + 2215: ones 2+5=7, tens 7+1=8, hundreds 4+2=6, thousands 2+2=4, giving 4687 kilograms of rice.

mcqs.q: There are 4256 motor bikes and 2639 bicycles in a city. How many are there altogether?
mcqs.why: Add 4256 + 2639: ones 6+9=15 write 5 carry 1, tens 5+3+1=9, hundreds 2+6=8, thousands 4+2=6, giving 6895 altogether.

mcqs.q: There are 3799 apples and 2405 mangoes in a shop. How many fruits are there altogether?
mcqs.why: Add 3799 + 2405 with carrying: ones 14 write 4 carry 1, tens 10 write 0 carry 1, hundreds 12 write 2 carry 1, thousands 6, giving 6204 fruits.

mcqs.q: Samad has 3492 goats and 509 cows. How many cattle does Samad have altogether?
mcqs.why: Add 3492 + 509 with carrying: ones 11 write 1 carry 1, tens 10 write 0 carry 1, hundreds 10 write 0 carry 1, thousands 4, giving 4001 cattle.

mcqs.q: Which operation do we use to find how many altogether in these word problems?
mcqs.why: Words like altogether and in two days mean we join the two amounts, so we add them together to find the total amount.
Add column by column: 0+5=5, 6+3=9, 3+2=5 and 2+1=3 in the thousands place, so 2360 + 1235 = 3595.

mcqs.q: In 4256 + 2639, what do we write in the ones place and what do we carry?
mcqs.why: Ones: 6 + 9 = 15. We cannot write 15 in one place, so we write 5 in the ones place and carry 1 ten to the tens column.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sold 2472 kg of rice in week 1. If the two-week total is 4687 kg, how much was sold in week 2?
mcqs.why: The notes give week 2 as 2215 kg, and checking: 2472 + 2215 = 4687, since 2+5=7, 7+1=8, 4+2=6 and 2+2=4.

lessons.title: Real-World Word Problems  -  Subtraction (page 56)

mcqs.q: A bookshop has 6666 books and 3498 are sold. How many books are left?
mcqs.why: Subtract the sold books: 6666 - 3498 = 3168. Regrouping is needed in the ones, tens and hundreds places to complete it.

mcqs.q: Faryal had Rs. 9656. She gave Rs. 8325 to her brother. How much money is left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 9656 - 8325: ones 6-5=1, tens 5-2=3, hundreds 6-3=3, thousands 9-8=1, so Rs. 1331 is left with Faryal.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper had 4834 packets of sweets and sold 2423 packets. How many packets are left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 4834 - 2423: ones 4-3=1, tens 3-2=1, hundreds 8-4=4, thousands 4-2=2, so 2411 packets are left.

mcqs.q: In an exam 6891 students appeared and 4371 passed. How many students failed?
mcqs.why: Failed = appeared - passed = 6891 - 4371: ones 1-1=0, tens 9-7=2, hundreds 8-3=5, thousands 6-4=2, giving 2520 students.

mcqs.q: Ahmed has Rs. 9180 and took out Rs. 3597. How much money is left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 9180 - 3597 with regrouping: ones 10-7=3, tens 17-9=8, hundreds 10-5=5, thousands 9-1-3=5, giving Rs. 5583 left.

mcqs.q: Sadia has Rs. 8000 and gave Rs. 4255 for Zakat. How much is left?
mcqs.why: Regroup 8000 as 7 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones. Then 10-5=5, 9-5=4, 9-2=7, 7-4=3, giving Rs. 3745 left.

mcqs.q: Which operation do we use to find how much is left in these word problems?
mcqs.why: Words like left, remaining and failed mean we take the smaller amount away from the bigger amount, so we use subtraction.
Work with regrouping from the ones place: 6666 - 3498 gives ones 8, tens 6, hundreds 1 and thousands 3, so the difference is 3168.

mcqs.q: In 8000 - 4255, 8000 is regrouped as which of these?
mcqs.why: To subtract across zeros, regroup step by step: 8000 becomes 7 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones before subtracting.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper had 4834 packets and 2411 are left. How many packets were sold?
mcqs.why: The notes give sold as 2423 packets, and checking: 4834 - 2423 = 2411, since 4-3=1, 3-2=1, 8-4=4 and 4-2=2.

lessons.notes_html:

options: To check if the exact answer is reasonable

lessons.notes_html:
Estimation is helpful when we are subtracting, to decide whether the answer is reasonable or not. Example (page 59): Arshad has 484 marbles. Qamar has 314 marbles. How many more marbles does Arshad have than Qamar? Solution: 484 - 314 = ? We have exact difference 484 - 314 = 170. We estimate the difference: 484 rounds to 500, 314 rounds to 300. We have exact difference 2892 - 2324 = 568. We find the estimated difference: 2892 rounds to 3000, 2324 rounds to 2000. Then, subtract the rounded numbers: 3000 - 2000 = 1000. So, the estimated difference is 1000.

lessons.title: Multiplication  -  Counting and writing in multiple steps (page 61)

mcqs.q: There are 3 pairs of shoes. How many shoes are there altogether?
mcqs.why: Each pair has 2 shoes, so add 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. This is also written as 3 times 2 = 6, or 3 x 2 = 6.

mcqs.q: What is 2 + 2 + 2 written as a multiplication?
mcqs.why: There are three 2s added together, so we write 3 times 2. That is 3 x 2 = 6, and 6 is called the product.

mcqs.q: What is 3 + 3 + 3?
mcqs.why: Add the three groups of 3 stars: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. This is also 3 times 3 = 9, written as 3 x 3 = 9.
There are eight 2s for the dots. Adding them gives 16, which is also 8 times 2 = 16, written as 8 x 2 = 16.

mcqs.q: What is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
mcqs.why: There are four 5s for the hearts. Adding gives 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20, which is 5 times 4 = 20, written as 5 x 4 = 20.

mcqs.q: What do we call the answer in multiplication?
mcqs.why: The notes say we can use the term product for the result of multiplication of two numbers, for example the product of 3 and 2 is 6.

mcqs.q: How do we read 3 x 2 = 6 in words?
mcqs.why: The sign x means times. The notes write 3 x 2 = 6 as 3 times 2 = 6, showing multiplication is repeated addition.

mcqs.q: Which addition shows 8 x 2?
mcqs.why: 8 x 2 means 2 added eight times. Writing all eight 2s and adding them gives 2+2+2+2+2+2+2+2 = 16.

mcqs.q: What is the product of 3 and 3?
mcqs.why: Multiply 3 by 3 using repeated addition: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. So the product of 3 and 3 is 9, written 3 x 3 = 9.

mcqs.q: What is the product of 5 and 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply 5 by 4 using repeated addition: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. So the product of 5 and 4 is 20, written 5 x 4 = 20.

lessons.notes_html: There are 3 pairs of shoes. How many shoes are there altogether? Number of pairs of shoes = 3. Number of shoes = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. We can write it as: 3 times 2 = 6, or 3 x 2 = 6, or the product of 3 and 2 is 6. So, we can use the term product for multiplication of two numbers. Few more examples are given below: Stars: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9; 3 times 3 = 9; 3 x 3 = 9. Dots: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 16; 8 times 2 = 16; 8 x 2 = 16. NOTE on the hearts example (page 61): the book's addition line prints five 5s (5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5) but gives the answer 20 and writes '5 times 4 = 20' and '5 x 4 = 20'. Five 5s would make 25, so the correct addition line is four 5s: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20, matching 5 times 4 = 20 and 5 x 4 = 20. The corrected line is used here.

lessons.title: Multiplication Tables (pages 62 to 65)

mcqs.q: What is 6 x 7?
mcqs.why: From the table of 6: 6 sevens are 42. Check by repeated addition: adding 6 seven times gives 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42.

mcqs.q: What is 6 x 9?
mcqs.why: From the table of 6: 6 nines are 54. The table of 6 goes 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 8?
mcqs.why: From the table of 7: 7 eights are 56. The table of 7 goes 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 5?
mcqs.why: From the table of 7: 7 fives are 35. Check: 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 = 35, adding 7 a total of five times.

mcqs.q: What is 8 x 6?
mcqs.why: From the table of 8: 8 sixes are 48. The table of 8 goes 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80.

mcqs.q: What is 8 x 9?
mcqs.why: From the table of 8: 8 nines are 72. Check in the table of 8: after 64 for 8 x 8 comes 72 for 8 x 9.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 7?
mcqs.why: From the table of 9: 9 sevens are 63. The table of 9 goes 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 9?
mcqs.why: From the table of 9: 9 nines are 81. Check: the table of 9 reaches 72 at 9 x 8 and then 81 at 9 x 9.

mcqs.q: What is 6 x 10?
mcqs.why: From the table of 6: 6 tens are 60. The table is built by repeated addition of 6, ending with 54 then 60 at ten times.

mcqs.q: What comes next in the table of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, ...?
mcqs.why: The table of 7 is built by adding 7 each time: 28 + 7 = 35. So after 28 comes 35, which is 7 x 5 = 35.

lessons.notes_html:

The table is built by repeated addition: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6, giving 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60.

The table is built by repeated addition: 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7, giving 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70.

lessons.title: Multiplication Sentence (page 66)

mcqs.q: Six groups of 2 stars make which multiplication sentence?
mcqs.why: Add 2 six times: 2+2+2+2+2+2 = 12. The multiplication sentence is 6 x 2 = 12, where 12 is the product.
There are six 2s. Adding them step by step: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. So the total is 12, as in 6 x 2 = 12.

mcqs.q: In 6 x 2 = 12, what is 12 called?
mcqs.why: In the multiplication sentence 6 x 2 = 12, the notes say 6 is a factor, 2 is a factor, and 12 is the product.

mcqs.q: In 6 x 2 = 12, what are 6 and 2 called?
mcqs.why: The notes say in 6 x 2 = 12, 6 is the factor and 2 is the factor, while the result 12 is called the product.

mcqs.q: 8 groups of 3 dots make which multiplication sentence?
mcqs.why: Add 3 eight times: 3+3+3+3+3+3+3+3 = 24. So the multiplication sentence is 8 x 3 = 24.

mcqs.q: 9 groups of 4 hearts make which multiplication sentence?
mcqs.why: Add 4 nine times: 4+4+4+4+4+4+4+4+4 = 36. So the multiplication sentence is 9 x 4 = 36.

mcqs.q: How do we say 6 x 2 = 12 in words?
options: Two multiplied by twelve is six
mcqs.why: The notes give the words for 6 x 2 = 12 as: Six multiplied by 2 is twelve. The product of 6 and 2 is 12.

mcqs.q: What is the product of 6 and 2?
mcqs.why: Multiply 6 by 2: add 2 six times to get 12, or add 6 two times: 6 + 6 = 12. So the product of 6 and 2 is 12.
There are eight 3s. Adding them gives 24, which matches the multiplication sentence 8 x 3 = 24 from the notes.
There are nine 4s. Adding them gives 36, which matches the multiplication sentence 9 x 4 = 36 from the notes.

lessons.notes_html:
Six groups of 2 stars: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 12. 6 times 2 equal to 12. 6 x 2 = 12 (Multiplication sentence). In the sentence, 6 is the Factor, 2 is the Factor, and 12 is the Product. Or in words: Six multiplied by 2 is twelve. Or in vertical form: 6 x 2 = 12. So, the product of 6 and 2 is 12.

lessons.title: Changing Order in Multiplication (page 67)

mcqs.q: What is 2 x 7?
mcqs.why: Multiply 2 by 7: 2 x 7 = 14. Changing the order gives 7 x 2 = 14 also, so the product stays the same.

mcqs.q: If 7 x 2 = 14, what is 2 x 7?
mcqs.why: Changing the order in multiplication does not change the product. Since 7 x 2 = 14, then 2 x 7 = 14 as well.

mcqs.q: What is 6 x 3?
mcqs.why: Multiply 6 by 3: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. Also 3 x 6 = 18, showing the product remains the same when order changes.

mcqs.q: What is 5 x 7?
mcqs.why: Multiply 5 by 7: from the tables, 7 x 5 = 35 and 5 x 7 = 35. Changing the order keeps the product the same.

mcqs.q: What is 8 x 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply 8 by 4: 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32. Also 4 x 8 = 32, so both orders give the same product of 32.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 2?
mcqs.why: Multiply 9 by 2: 9 + 9 = 18. Also 2 x 9 = 18, showing changing the order does not change the product.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 6?
mcqs.why: Multiply 7 by 6: from the tables, 7 x 6 = 42 and 6 x 7 = 42. Both orders give the same product of 42.

mcqs.q: What is 8 x 6?
mcqs.why: Multiply 8 by 6: from the tables, 8 x 6 = 48 and 6 x 8 = 48. Changing the order keeps the product the same.

mcqs.q: What happens to the product when we change the order in multiplication?
mcqs.why: The notes say: if we change the order in multiplication the product remains the same, for example 2 x 6 = 6 x 2 = 12.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 7?
mcqs.why: Multiply 9 by 7: from the tables, 9 x 7 = 63 and 7 x 9 = 63. Both orders give the same product of 63.

lessons.notes_html:
Example (page 67): Multiply 7 and 2 (change order). Solution: 2 x 7 = 14 and 7 x 2 = 14. So, 2 x 7 = 7 x 2. Example (page 67): Multiply 6 and 2 (change order). Solution: 2 x 6 = 12 and 6 x 2 = 12. So, if we change the order in multiplication the product remains the same.

mcqs.why: Ones: 2 x 7 = 14, write 4 regroup 1 ten. Tens: 6 x 7 = 42 tens, plus 1 ten = 43. So 62 x 7 = 434.

mcqs.why: Ones: 4 x 7 = 28, write 8 regroup 2 tens. Tens: 2 x 7 = 14 tens, plus 2 = 16 tens. So 24 x 7 = 168.

mcqs.q: What is 30 x 8?
mcqs.why: Ones: 0 x 8 = 0. Tens: 3 x 8 = 24 tens, write 4 in tens and 2 in hundreds. So 30 x 8 = 240.

mcqs.q: What is 45 x 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 x 9 = 45, write 5 regroup 4 tens. Tens: 4 x 9 = 36 tens, plus 4 = 40 tens. So 45 x 9 = 405.

mcqs.q: What is 88 x 6?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 x 6 = 48, write 8 regroup 4 tens. Tens: 8 x 6 = 48 tens, plus 4 = 52 tens. So 88 x 6 = 528.

mcqs.q: Using the splitting method, what is 26 x 5?

i. Let us multiply 26 and 5 using mental calculation method by splitting up or distribution numbers. 26 x 5 = (20 + 6) x 5 (Splitting 26 = 20 + 6) = (20 x 5) + (6 x 5) = 100 + 30 = 130. ii. Now we multiply 48 x 3 using mental calculation method by rounding off one of them to nearest 10. 48 can be rounded off to the nearest 10, which is 50. We multiply 50 x 3 = 150. lessons.title: Division (page 73)

mcqs.q: 14 balls are divided into 2 equal groups. How many balls are in each group?
mcqs.why: 14 balls shared into 2 equal groups: 14 / 2 = 7, because 2 groups of 7 make 14. So each of the 2 groups has 7 balls.

mcqs.q: What is 14 / 7?
mcqs.why: Group the 14 balls into 2 equal groups of 7 balls each. The number of groups is 2, so 14 / 7 = 2.

mcqs.q: What is 7 / 14?
mcqs.why: Dividing 7 balls among 14 equal groups gives less than one whole ball in each group: 7 / 14 = 1/2, which is not the same as 14 / 7.

options: Only when both numbers are the same
No, the order cannot be changed in division
mcqs.q: In division, can we change the order of the numbers and get the same answer?
mcqs.why: No. The lesson shows 14 / 7 = 2 but 7 / 14 = 1/2. Since 2 is not equal to 1/2, changing the order changes the answer.

mcqs.q: What does the lesson say about 14 / 7 and 7 / 14?
mcqs.why: 14 / 7 = 2, while 7 / 14 = 1/2. Because 2 and 1/2 are different, the two divisions are not equal.

mcqs.q: If 7 balls are divided into 14 equal groups, how much does each group get?
mcqs.why: There are only 7 balls for 14 groups, so each group gets less than one whole ball: 7 / 14 = 1/2 of a ball each.

mcqs.q: When 14 balls are grouped so that each group has 7 balls, how many groups are formed?
mcqs.why: Count groups of 7 in 14: 7 + 7 = 14, which makes 2 groups. This is why 14 / 7 = 2.

mcqs.q: Which statement is TRUE about division?
mcqs.why: Division cannot be done in any order: 10 / 2 = 5 but 2 / 10 is less than 1, so they are not equal, just like 14 / 7 and 7 / 14.

mcqs.q: What is 12 / 4?
mcqs.why: Group 12 into groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 makes 3 groups, so 12 / 4 = 3.

mcqs.q: A student says 12 / 4 and 4 / 12 give the same answer. What is correct?
mcqs.why: 12 / 4 = 3, but 4 / 12 is less than 1 because 4 items cannot fill 12 whole groups. The order matters, so they are not the same.

lessons.notes_html: Division of any two numbers cannot be done in any order. In division we cannot change the order. 14 / 7 and 7 / 14 are not the same. Scenario 1: Divide 14 by 7. Group the 14 balls into 2 equal groups. Each group will have 7 balls. So, 14 / 7 = 2. Scenario 2: Divide 7 / 14. Try to divide 7 balls into 14 equal groups. Each group will have less than 1/2 a ball each, which may be hard to represent with physical objects. So, 7 / 14 = 1/2, which is not the same as 14 / 7 = 2. So, in division we cannot change the order: 14 / 7 is not equal to 7 / 14.

lessons.title: Division of 2-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers (with and without remainder) (pages 74 to 75)

mcqs.q: What is 69 / 3?
mcqs.why: Divide the tens first: 6 / 3 = 2, write 2 in the tens place. Bring down 9 ones: 9 / 3 = 3. So 69 / 3 = 23.

mcqs.q: What is 72 / 6?
mcqs.why: 6 into 7 goes 1 time with remainder 1. Bring down 2 to make 12. 12 / 6 = 2. So 72 / 6 = 12.

mcqs.q: What is 93 / 7?
mcqs.why: Tens: 9 / 7 = 1, remainder 2 tens. Bring down 3 to make 23. 23 / 7 = 3 remainder 2, since 7 x 3 = 21. Answer: 13 remainder 2.

mcqs.q: What is 80 / 6?
mcqs.why: Tens: 8 / 6 = 1, remainder 2 tens. Bring down 0 to make 20. 20 / 6 = 3 remainder 2, since 6 x 3 = 18. Answer: 13 remainder 2.

mcqs.q: In 11 / 5 = 2 remainder 1, what is the 1 called?
mcqs.why: In division, the number left over after dividing is the remainder. Here 5 x 2 = 10, and 11 - 10 = 1 is left over.

mcqs.q: In a division, the number being divided is called what?
mcqs.why: The number being divided is the dividend. The number we divide by is the divisor, the answer is the quotient, and what is left over is the remainder.

mcqs.q: What is 33 / 5?
mcqs.why: 5 x 6 = 30, which is the largest multiple of 5 not bigger than 33. 33 - 30 = 3 is left over. So 33 / 5 = 6 remainder 3.

mcqs.q: What is 65 / 4?
mcqs.why: Tens: 6 / 4 = 1, remainder 2. Bring down 5 to make 25. 25 / 4 = 6 remainder 1, since 4 x 6 = 24. Answer: 16 remainder 1.

mcqs.q: What is 95 / 3?
mcqs.why: Tens: 9 / 3 = 3. Bring down 5: 5 / 3 = 1 remainder 2, since 3 x 1 = 3 and 5 - 3 = 2. Answer: 31 remainder 2.

mcqs.q: What is 89 / 4?
mcqs.why: Tens: 8 / 4 = 2. Bring down 9: 9 / 4 = 2 remainder 1, since 4 x 2 = 8 and 9 - 8 = 1. Answer: 22 remainder 1.

lessons.notes_html:
Example (page 74): Divide 69 by 3. Divide a 2-digit number with a 1-digit number by long division. Divide the tens first: 6 / 3 = 2. Write down 2 as quotient in tens place. Then bring down 9 ones from dividend. Divide the number in ones place: 9 / 3 = 3. Write 3 as quotient in ones place. So, 69 / 3 = 23. Example (page 74): (i) 72 / 6. Long division: 6 into 7 goes 1 time, remainder 1; bring down 2 to make 12; 12 / 6 = 2. So 72 / 6 = 12. Key note (page 74): In the Division Process, the number being divided is the Dividend, the number we divide by is the Divisor, the answer is the Quotient, and what is left over is the Remainder (example in the book: 11 / 5 = 2 remainder 1).

mcqs.q: What is 684 / 6?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 6 / 6 = 1. Tens: 8 / 6 = 1, leaving 2 tens. Bring down 4 to make 24. Ones: 24 / 6 = 4. So 684 / 6 = 114.

mcqs.q: What is 455 / 5?
mcqs.why: 4 hundreds cannot be divided by 5, so divide 45 tens: 45 / 5 = 9. Bring down 5 ones: 5 / 5 = 1. So 455 / 5 = 91.

mcqs.q: What is 643 / 6?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 6 / 6 = 1. Tens: 4 tens cannot be divided by 6, so bring down 3 to make 43. 43 / 6 = 7 remainder 1, since 6 x 7 = 42. Answer: 107 remainder 1.

mcqs.q: What is 848 / 4?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 8 / 4 = 2. Tens: 4 / 4 = 1. Ones: 8 / 4 = 2. Putting the digits together, 848 / 4 = 212.

mcqs.q: What is 784 / 7?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 7 / 7 = 1. Tens: 8 / 7 = 1 remainder 1. Bring down 4 to make 14. 14 / 7 = 2. So 784 / 7 = 112.

mcqs.q: What is 968 / 8?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 9 / 8 = 1 remainder 1. Bring down 6 to make 16: 16 / 8 = 2. Ones: 8 / 8 = 1. So 968 / 8 = 121.

mcqs.q: What is 421 / 9?
mcqs.why: 42 tens / 9 = 4 remainder 6 tens, since 9 x 4 = 36. Bring down 1 to make 61. 61 / 9 = 6 remainder 7, since 9 x 6 = 54. Answer: 46 remainder 7.

mcqs.q: What is 835 / 7?
mcqs.why: 83 / 7 = 11 remainder 6, since 7 x 11 = 77. Bring down 5 to make 65. 65 / 7 = 9 remainder 2, since 7 x 9 = 63. Answer: 119 remainder 2.

mcqs.q: What is 209 / 8?
mcqs.why: 20 / 8 = 2 remainder 4, since 8 x 2 = 16. Bring down 9 to make 49. 49 / 8 = 6 remainder 1, since 8 x 6 = 48. Answer: 26 remainder 1.

mcqs.q: What is 999 / 9?
mcqs.why: Hundreds: 9 / 9 = 1. Tens: 9 / 9 = 1. Ones: 9 / 9 = 1. Putting the digits together, 999 / 9 = 111.

lessons.title: Divide Mentally (page 78)

mcqs.q: Divide mentally by splitting: what is 35 / 5?
mcqs.why: Split 35 = 30 + 5. Divide each part by 5: 30 / 5 = 6 and 5 / 5 = 1. Add them: 6 + 1 = 7, so 35 / 5 = 7.

mcqs.q: To divide 35 by 5 mentally, 35 is split into which two numbers in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson splits 35 = 30 + 5, because both 30 and 5 divide exactly by 5: 30 / 5 = 6 and 5 / 5 = 1.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 63 / 7?
mcqs.why: Recall the 7 times table: 7 x 9 = 63, so dividing back, 63 / 7 = 9. Check: 9 groups of 7 make 63.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 72 / 9?
mcqs.why: Recall the 9 times table: 9 x 8 = 72, so dividing back, 72 / 9 = 8. Check: 8 groups of 9 make 72.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 690 / 6?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 6 x 115 = 690, because 6 x 100 = 600 and 6 x 15 = 90, and 600 + 90 = 690. So 690 / 6 = 115.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 496 / 4?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 4 x 124 = 496, because 4 x 100 = 400 and 4 x 24 = 96, and 400 + 96 = 496. So 496 / 4 = 124.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 917 / 7?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 7 x 131 = 917, because 7 x 130 = 910 and 910 + 7 = 917. So 917 / 7 = 131.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 785 / 5?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 5 x 157 = 785, because 5 x 150 = 750 and 5 x 7 = 35, and 750 + 35 = 785. So 785 / 5 = 157.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 972 / 6?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 6 x 162 = 972, because 6 x 160 = 960 and 6 x 2 = 12, and 960 + 12 = 972. So 972 / 6 = 162.

mcqs.q: Divide mentally: what is 896 / 8?
mcqs.why: Check by multiplication: 8 x 112 = 896, because 8 x 100 = 800 and 8 x 12 = 96, and 800 + 96 = 896. So 896 / 8 = 112.

lessons.title: Dividing a number by 1 and itself (page 79)

mcqs.q: What is 5 / 1?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by 1 is the number itself. Dividing 5 by 1 keeps it as one group of 5, so 5 / 1 = 5.

mcqs.q: What is 8 / 8?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by itself is 1. Here 8 divided into groups of 8 makes exactly 1 group, so 8 / 8 = 1.

mcqs.q: What is 7 / 1?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by 1 is the number itself, because dividing by 1 does not split the number at all. So 7 / 1 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is 9 / 9?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by itself is always 1. Here 9 divided into one group of 9 gives exactly 1 group, so 9 / 9 = 1.

mcqs.q: What is 0 / 1?
mcqs.why: Zero divided by 1 is 0, because there is nothing to share out: 0 items put into 1 group still gives 0 items in the group.

mcqs.q: What number is missing: 5 / _____ = 1?
mcqs.why: A number divided by itself gives 1. So the missing number must equal 5 itself: 5 / 5 = 1, so the missing number is 5.

mcqs.q: What number is missing: _____ / 2 = 1?
mcqs.why: For the answer to be 1, the number must be divided by itself. So the missing number is 2, because 2 / 2 = 1.

mcqs.q: What number is missing: _____ / 1 = 1?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by 1 is the number itself. For the answer to be 1, the starting number must be 1, because 1 / 1 = 1.

mcqs.q: What is 7 / 7?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by itself is 1. Here 7 divided into groups of 7 makes exactly 1 group, so 7 / 7 = 1.

mcqs.q: What is 3 / 1?
mcqs.why: Any number divided by 1 is the number itself, because dividing by 1 leaves the number unchanged. So 3 / 1 = 3.

lessons.title: Real-World Word Problems  -  Division (page 80)

mcqs.q: Raheel had 42 seeds and 7 pots. How many seeds did he plant in each pot?
mcqs.why: Divide the seeds equally among the pots: 42 / 7 = 6, because 7 x 6 = 42. So he planted 6 seeds in each pot.

mcqs.q: Sheraz divided Rs. 90 equally among 6 boys. How much money did each boy get?
mcqs.why: Divide 90 / 6. Since 6 x 15 = 90, the quotient is 15. So each boy got Rs. 15.

mcqs.q: A tailor has 96 buttons. If he sews 8 buttons on each shirt, how many shirts can he sew?
mcqs.why: Divide 96 / 8. Since 8 x 12 = 96, the quotient is 12. So the tailor can sew 12 shirts.

mcqs.q: A book contains 387 pages. Akram reads 9 pages in a day. How many days are required to read the book?
mcqs.why: Divide 387 / 9. Since 9 x 43 = 387, the quotient is 43. So Akram needs 43 days to read the book.

mcqs.q: One pencil costs Rs. 6. How many pencils can be bought for Rs. 468?
mcqs.why: Divide 468 / 6. Since 6 x 78 = 468, the quotient is 78. So 78 pencils can be bought for Rs. 468.

mcqs.q: There are 7 days in a week. How many weeks are there in 364 days?
mcqs.why: Divide 364 / 7. Since 7 x 52 = 364, the quotient is 52. So there are 52 weeks in 364 days.

mcqs.q: In a school 992 students stood in 8 rows. How many students were there in one row?
mcqs.why: Divide 992 / 8. Since 8 x 124 = 992, the quotient is 124. So there were 124 students in one row.

mcqs.q: Which multiplication checks the answer to 387 / 9 = 43?
mcqs.why: Division is checked by multiplying the quotient by the divisor: 9 x 43 = 387, which equals the dividend, so 387 / 9 = 43 is correct.

mcqs.q: Sheraz divided Rs. 90 equally among 6 boys. Which amount shows what EACH boy got?
mcqs.why: Sharing equally means dividing: 90 / 6 = 15, because 6 x 15 = 90. The amount each boy got is Rs. 15, not the total Rs. 90.

mcqs.q: In a school 992 students stood in 8 equal rows. How many ROWS were there?
mcqs.why: The problem already tells us the students stood in 8 rows; dividing 992 / 8 = 124 gives the students in one row, not the number of rows.

lessons.title: Real-World Word Problems  -  Mixed Operations (page 81)

mcqs.q: There are 4573 men and 3112 women in a village. What is the total population of the village?
mcqs.why: Add 4573 + 3112 place by place: ones 3 + 2 = 5, tens 7 + 1 = 8, hundreds 5 + 1 = 6, thousands 4 + 3 = 7. Total = 7685 people.

mcqs.q: Sara bought 2 sarees for Rs. 3250 and Rs. 2550. How much money did she spend in all?
mcqs.why: Add 3250 + 2550: ones 0, tens 5 + 5 = 10 write 0 carry 1, hundreds 2 + 5 + 1 = 8, thousands 3 + 2 = 5. Total = Rs. 5800.

mcqs.q: A nursery planted 3438 red flowers and 2394 yellow flowers. How many flowers were planted in all?
mcqs.why: Add 3438 + 2394: ones 8 + 4 = 12 write 2 carry 1, tens 3 + 9 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1, hundreds 4 + 3 + 1 = 8, thousands 3 + 2 = 5. Total = 5832 flowers.

mcqs.q: There are 4865 students in a school. If 2746 are boys, how many girls are there?
mcqs.why: Subtract 4865 - 2746: ones 15 - 6 = 9 after regrouping, tens 6 - 1 - 4 = 1, hundreds 8 - 7 = 1, thousands 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 2119 girls.

mcqs.q: A bakery had 3596 buns. 2767 buns were sold. How many buns were left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 3596 - 2767: ones 16 - 7 = 9, tens 9 - 1 - 6 = 2, hundreds 15 - 7 = 8 after regrouping, thousands 3 - 1 - 2 = 0. Answer: 829 buns left.

mcqs.q: A milkman carried 2585 bottles of milk. He delivered 1431 bottles. How many bottles were left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 2585 - 1431 place by place: ones 5 - 1 = 4, tens 8 - 3 = 5, hundreds 5 - 4 = 1, thousands 2 - 1 = 1. Answer: 1154 bottles left.

mcqs.q: There are 75 chairs in a hall. How many chairs are there in 6 such halls?
mcqs.why: Multiply 75 x 6: ones 5 x 6 = 30 write 0 regroup 3, tens 7 x 6 = 42 plus 3 = 45. Answer: 450 chairs in 6 halls.

mcqs.q: In a factory 84 school bags are made in one day. How many bags will be made in 8 days?
mcqs.why: Multiply 84 x 8: ones 4 x 8 = 32 write 2 regroup 3, tens 8 x 8 = 64 plus 3 = 67. Answer: 672 bags in 8 days.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sells 125 umbrellas in a day. How many umbrellas will he sell in 7 days?
mcqs.why: Multiply 125 x 7: ones 35 write 5 regroup 3, tens 14 + 3 = 17 write 7 regroup 1, hundreds 7 + 1 = 8. Answer: 875 umbrellas.

mcqs.q: There are 147 books. 7 books are placed on each shelf. How many shelves are there?
mcqs.why: Divide 147 / 7. Since 7 x 21 = 147, the quotient is 21. Answer: 21 shelves are needed for the books.

lessons.title: Numbers Patterns (page 82)

mcqs.q: Complete the pattern: 302, 304, 306, 308, 310, _____
mcqs.why: The pattern increases by 2 each time: 302, 304, 306, 308, 310. Adding 2 to 310 gives the next number, 312.

mcqs.q: Complete the pattern: 459, 457, 455, 453, 451, _____
mcqs.why: The pattern decreases by 2 each time: 459, 457, 455, 453, 451. Subtracting 2 from 451 gives the next number, 449.

mcqs.q: Complete the pattern: 515, 525, 535, 545, 555, _____
mcqs.why: The pattern increases by 10 each time: 515, 525, 535, 545, 555. Adding 10 to 555 gives the next number, 565.

mcqs.q: Complete the pattern: 750, 740, 730, 720, 710, _____
mcqs.why: The pattern decreases by 10 each time: 750, 740, 730, 720, 710. Subtracting 10 from 710 gives the next number, 700.
The pattern increases by 100 each time: 9050, 9150, 9250, 9350, 9450. Adding 100 to 9450 gives the next number, 9550.

mcqs.q: What is the rule of the pattern 302, 304, 306, 308, 310?
mcqs.why: Each number is 2 more than the one before it: 304 - 302 = 2 and 306 - 304 = 2. So the pattern is increasing by 2.
The pattern increases by 10: 110, 120, then 120 + 10 = 130, then 140 and 150. So the missing number is 130.
The pattern decreases by 10 each time: 500, 490, 480, then 480 - 10 = 470, then 460 and 450. So the number in the gap is 470.
The pattern decreases by 10: 550, 540, then 540 - 10 = 530, then 520. So the missing number in the gap is 530.

mcqs.q: What is the rule of the pattern 9050, 9150, 9250, 9350, 9450?
mcqs.why: Each number is 100 more than the one before it: 9150 - 9050 = 100 and 9250 - 9150 = 100. So the pattern is increasing by 100.

lessons.title: Numbers Patterns  -  Finding the Missing Number (page 83)

mcqs.q: Find the missing number: 20 + w = 100. What is w?
mcqs.why: Use the inverse operation: subtract 20 from 100. 100 - 20 = 80. Check: 20 + 80 = 100, so w = 80.

mcqs.q: Find the missing number: 45 - x = 32. What is x?
mcqs.why: For a subtraction sentence, swap and subtract: 45 - 32 = 13. Check: 45 - 13 = 32, so x = 13.

mcqs.q: Complete the number sentence: 4 + _____ = 9
mcqs.why: Use the inverse operation: 9 - 4 = 5. Check: 4 + 5 = 9, so the missing number is 5.

mcqs.q: Which operation completes the sentence: 19 _____ 14 = 5?
mcqs.why: Try subtraction: 19 - 14 = 5, which is correct. Adding gives 33, multiplying gives 266, and dividing does not give 5.

mcqs.q: Which operation completes the sentence: 20 _____ 5 = 4?
mcqs.why: Try division: 20 / 5 = 4, which is correct. Adding gives 25, subtracting gives 15, and multiplying gives 100.

mcqs.q: Complete the number sentence: _____ / 4 = 4
mcqs.why: Use the inverse operation: multiply 4 x 4 = 16. Check: 16 / 4 = 4, so the missing number is 16.

mcqs.q: Complete the number sentence: 15 - _____ = 9
mcqs.why: For a subtraction sentence, swap and subtract: 15 - 9 = 6. Check: 15 - 6 = 9, so the missing number is 6.

mcqs.q: Complete the number sentence: _____ + 18 = 30
mcqs.why: Use the inverse operation: 30 - 18 = 12. Check: 12 + 18 = 30, so the missing number is 12.

mcqs.q: Which operation completes the sentence: 30 _____ 6 = 5?
mcqs.why: Try division: 30 / 6 = 5, which is correct, because 6 x 5 = 30. The other operations give 36, 24, and 180.

mcqs.q: Complete the number sentence: _____ x 8 = 64
mcqs.why: Use the inverse operation: divide 64 / 8 = 8. Check: 8 x 8 = 64, so the missing number is 8.

lessons.notes_html:
To find the missing numbers use the inverse operation. Example (page 83): 20 + w = 100. Solution: Inverse step: 100 - 20. So, w = 80 (missing number). If the missing number is in a subtraction sentence, swap the numbers and subtract. Example (page 83): 45 - x = 32. Solution: Inverse step: 45 - 32. So, x = 13 (missing number). Finding missing number or operation. Example (page 83): Complete the number sentences: a) 19 ___ 14 = 5, b) 20 ___ 5 = 4. Solution: a) 19 - 14 = 5, b) 20 / 5 = 4.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Summary (page 84)

options: Add all digits together in any order
Add ones to ones, tens to tens, hundreds to hundreds and thousands to thousands
Add thousands first, then guess the rest
mcqs.q: When adding numbers, how should the digits be added?
mcqs.why: The summary says to add place by place: ones with ones, tens with tens, hundreds with hundreds, and thousands with thousands, carrying when a place makes 10 or more.

mcqs.q: When zero is subtracted from any number, what is the answer?
mcqs.why: The summary says subtracting zero leaves the number unchanged: for example 47 - 0 = 47, because taking away nothing changes nothing.

mcqs.q: When a number is multiplied by 0, what is the answer always?
mcqs.why: The summary says any number times 0 is always 0: for example 35 x 0 = 0, because zero groups of a number make nothing.

mcqs.q: When a number is multiplied by 1, what is the answer always?
mcqs.why: The summary says any number times 1 is the number itself: for example 24 x 1 = 24, because one group of 24 is just 24.

mcqs.q: What happens when we change the order of numbers in multiplication?
mcqs.why: The summary says the product remains the same: for example 4 x 5 = 20 and 5 x 4 = 20, so changing the order does not change the answer.

options: Yes, the answer stays the same
No, we cannot change the order in division
mcqs.q: Can we change the order of numbers in division?
mcqs.why: The summary says in division we cannot change the order: 14 / 7 = 2 but 7 / 14 = 1/2, and 2 is not equal to 1/2.

mcqs.q: When a number is divided by itself, what is the answer always?
mcqs.why: The summary says a number divided by itself is always 1: for example 9 / 9 = 1, because 9 makes exactly one group of 9.

mcqs.q: In division vocabulary, what is the amount left over called?
mcqs.why: The summary vocabulary lists remainder as the part left over after dividing: for example in 11 / 5 = 2 remainder 1, the 1 left over is the remainder.

mcqs.q: In division vocabulary, what is the number being divided called?
mcqs.why: The number being divided is the dividend. In 11 / 5, the 11 is the dividend, 5 is the divisor, 2 is the quotient, and 1 is the remainder.

mcqs.q: In multiplication vocabulary, what is the answer to a multiplication called?
mcqs.why: The answer to a multiplication is the product: for example in 6 x 7 = 42, the number 42 is the product of 6 and 7.

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • When adding numbers, always add ones to ones, tens to tens, hundreds to hundreds and thousands to thousands.
  • Whenever zero is subtracted from any number, the answer is the number itself.
  • When multiply a number by 0, the answer is always 0.
  • When multiply a number by 1, the answer is always the number itself.
  • Whenever change the order in multiplication the product remains the same.
  • In division, we cannot change the order.
  • When a number is divided by itself, the answer is always 1.
  • Vocabulary: Thousands, estimating, odd sums, differences, multiple, multiplication sentence, divisor, dividend, remainder, product, groups, patterns.
  • This closes Unit 2 (pages 36 to 84).

lessons.title: Fractions (page 86)

mcqs.q: What is a fraction?
options: A number that shows parts of a whole
A number used only for counting
mcqs.why: The notes say a fraction is a number that shows parts of a whole, like parts of an object or parts of a group.

mcqs.q: A hexagon is divided into 6 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
mcqs.why: Shaded parts are written on top and total parts below: 3 shaded parts out of 6 equal parts gives the fraction 3/6.

mcqs.q: In the fraction 3/6, what is the numerator?
mcqs.why: The numerator is the number above the line. In 3/6 the number above the line is 3, so the numerator is 3.

mcqs.q: In the fraction 3/6, what is the denominator?
mcqs.why: The denominator is the number below the line. In 3/6 the number below the line is 6, so the denominator is 6.

mcqs.q: What does the numerator of a fraction tell us?
options: How many parts are in the whole
How many parts are being used
The size of the whole object
mcqs.why: The notes say the numerator tells how many parts are being used, while the denominator tells how many parts the whole has.

mcqs.q: What does the denominator of a fraction tell us?
options: How many parts are being used
How many parts are shaded only
How many parts are of a whole
mcqs.why: The denominator tells how many equal parts the whole has been divided into, that is, how many parts are of a whole.

mcqs.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal parts. One part is taken. What fraction of the pizza is taken?
mcqs.why: One part taken out of 4 equal parts is written with 1 on top and 4 below, giving the fraction 1/4 of the pizza.

mcqs.q: Which is greater: one half of a pizza or one quarter of the same pizza?
mcqs.why: The unit opener shows one half is greater than one quarter, because 1/2 covers more of the pizza than 1/4 does.

mcqs.q: Which symbol correctly compares 1/2 and 1/4?
mcqs.why: One half is greater than one quarter, as shown with the pizza, so we write 1/2 > 1/4 using the greater than symbol.

mcqs.q: A whole is divided into 3 equal parts. How many equal parts are there in the whole?
mcqs.why: The notes show a whole divided into 2, 3 and 4 equal parts. Divided into 3 means the whole has 3 equal parts.

lessons.notes_html:
Learning Outcomes

Students' Learning Outcomes (page 85): Recognise as proper fractions, improper fractions, mixed numbers. Identify equivalent fractions and show families of equivalent fractions. Simplify fractions to the lowest term. Compare and order like fractions using symbols <, > and =. Add and subtract like and unlike fractions (with denominators that are multiples of the same number). Know and recognise that hundredths arise by dividing an object, single digit numbers and quantities into hundred equal parts. Identify that tenths arise by dividing an object, single digit number and quantities into ten equal parts (e.g., 2/10 = 0.2). The unit opener shows a pizza: one half is greater than one quarter, and one quarter is less than one half.

A fraction is a number that shows parts of a whole. A fraction or common fraction is a number that means parts of an object or parts of a group. A pizza is shown as a Whole, then divided into 2 equal parts, 3 equal parts and 4 equal parts. Numerator and Denominator of a Fraction (page 86): Observe the figure - a hexagon with 3 of its 6 parts shaded, so 3/6 parts of the figure are shaded. Number 3 shows the total shaded parts of a whole. Number 6 shows the total equal parts into which the whole has been divided. Number 3 above the line is known as numerator. Number 6 below the line is known as denominator. Hence, in the fraction, the numerator is 3 and the denominator is 6. The numerator tells how many parts are being used. The denominator tells how many parts are of a whole.

lessons.title: Unit Fraction, Like Fractions, Unlike Fractions (page 87)

mcqs.q: What is a unit fraction?
options: A fraction with numerator greater than denominator
mcqs.why: The notes say one part of the whole is called a unit fraction, for example 1/2 is one part out of two equal parts.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a unit fraction?
mcqs.why: A unit fraction has 1 as its numerator, showing one part. In 1/9 the numerator is 1, so 1/9 is a unit fraction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a unit fraction?
mcqs.why: Unit fractions have numerator 1, like 1/2, 1/5 and 1/12. The fraction 2/6 has numerator 2, so it is not a unit fraction.

mcqs.q: Fractions with the same denominators are called what?
mcqs.why: The notes define like fractions as fractions with the same denominators, for example 1/4 and 3/4 both have denominator 4.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows like fractions?
mcqs.why: Like fractions have the same denominator. Both 2/6 and 5/6 have denominator 6, so they are like fractions.

mcqs.q: Fractions with different denominators are called what?
mcqs.why: The notes define unlike fractions as fractions with different denominators, for example 1/2 and 1/3 have denominators 2 and 3.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows unlike fractions?
mcqs.why: Unlike fractions have different denominators. The pair 2/5 and 4/8 has denominators 5 and 8, which are different.

mcqs.q: Are 5/10 and 3/10 like fractions or unlike fractions?
options: Like fractions, because both denominators are 10
Unit fractions, because numerators are small
Mixed fractions, because there are two fractions
mcqs.why: Both fractions have the same denominator 10. Fractions with the same denominators are like fractions, so 5/10 and 3/10 are like.

mcqs.q: What is the numerator of the unit fraction 1/5?
mcqs.why: The numerator is the number above the line. In the unit fraction 1/5 the number above the line is 1.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is a unit fraction from the notes?
mcqs.why: The notes list 1/2, 1/3, 1/5, 1/9 and 1/12 as unit fractions because each has numerator 1, showing one part of the whole.

lessons.notes_html: Unit Fraction: One part of the whole is called unit fraction. Examples: 1/2, 1/3, 1/5, 1/9, 1/12. Like Fractions: Fractions with the same denominators are called like fractions. Examples: 1/4 and 3/4; 2/6 and 5/6; 5/10 and 3/10. Unlike Fractions: Fractions with different denominators are called unlike fractions. Examples: 1/2 and 1/3; 2/3 and 2/6; 2/5 and 4/8.

lessons.title: Proper and Improper Fractions and Mixed Fractions (pages 88 to 89)

mcqs.q: A fraction with the numerator smaller than its denominator is called what?
mcqs.why: The notes say a fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator is a proper fraction, for example in 3/5, 3 is smaller than 5.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a proper fraction?
mcqs.why: In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator. In 2/5, 2 is smaller than 5, so 2/5 is proper.

mcqs.q: A fraction with the numerator greater than or equal to its denominator is called what?
mcqs.why: The notes say a fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator is an improper fraction, like 8/5.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an improper fraction?
mcqs.why: In an improper fraction the numerator is greater than or equal to the denominator. In 4/3, 4 is greater than 3, so it is improper.

mcqs.q: Why is 6/6 an improper fraction?
options: Because the numerator is equal to the denominator
mcqs.why: An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to the denominator. In 6/6 the numerator 6 equals the denominator 6.

mcqs.q: What is a mixed number?
options: A combination of a whole number and a proper fraction
A fraction with equal numerator and denominator
mcqs.why: The notes say a mixed number is the combination of a whole number and a proper fraction, for example 2 3/4 combines 2 and 3/4.

mcqs.q: In the mixed number 2 3/4, what is the whole number part?
mcqs.why: The mixed number 2 3/4 is the sum of whole number 2 and proper fraction 3/4, so the whole number part is 2.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a mixed fraction?
mcqs.why: A mixed fraction combines a whole number with a proper fraction. Only 5 3/7 has whole number 5 with fraction 3/7.

mcqs.q: Is 5/7 a proper fraction or an improper fraction?
options: Proper fraction, because 5 is smaller than 7
Improper fraction, because 5 is greater than 7
Mixed fraction, because it has two numbers
Unit fraction, because it shows one part
mcqs.why: Compare numerator and denominator: 5 is smaller than 7, and a numerator smaller than the denominator makes a proper fraction.

mcqs.q: From 3/6, 5/4, 1/2 and 8/7, which are the improper fractions?
mcqs.why: Improper fractions have numerator greater than or equal to denominator: 5 is greater than 4 in 5/4 and 8 is greater than 7 in 8/7.

lessons.notes_html:
Proper Fraction (page 88): A fraction with the numerator smaller than its denominator is called proper fraction. For example: 1/2, 2/4, 3/5, 2/5. In 1/2, 2/4, 3/5, 2/5, the numerator is smaller than the denominator. Hence these fractions are proper fractions. Improper Fraction (page 88): A fraction with the numerator greater than or equal to its denominator is called improper fraction. Examples: 8/5 and 5/3. Few more examples are: 4/3, 5/4, 6/6. NOTE - the book's list of 'few more examples' also prints 5/7, but 5/7 has a numerator smaller than its denominator, so it is a PROPER fraction, not an improper one; it is left out of the improper list here. Example (page 88): Write proper and improper fractions separately: 3/6, 7/10, 5/4, 9/3, 1/2, 2/6, 8/7, 11/4, 4/5. Proper fractions: 3/6, 7/10, 1/2, 2/6, 4/5. Improper fractions: 5/4, 9/3, 8/7, 11/4.

Mixed Numbers (Fractions) (page 89): A mixed number / fraction is the combination of a whole number and a proper fraction. For example, 2 3/4. We can show it as: 1 + 1 + 3/4 = 2 + 3/4 = 2 3/4. Mixed number (fraction) 2 3/4 is the sum of whole number 2 and proper fraction 3/4. Key note: We can convert an improper fraction into a mixed number (fraction) and a mixed number into an improper fraction. Example (page 89): Write mixed fractions separately, from: 1 1/2, 2 1/4, 1 1/4, 7/11, 4/5, 2 1/6, 5/13, 5 3/7. Mixed fractions: 1 1/2, 2 1/4, 1 1/4, 2 1/6, 5 3/7. NOTE - the book's printed solution lists only 1 1/4, 2 1/6 and 5 3/7, leaving out 1 1/2 and 2 1/4, which are also mixed fractions; the complete set is given here.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions (page 91)

mcqs.q: What are equivalent fractions?
options: Fractions with the same denominator only
Fractions having the same value but different numerators and denominators
mcqs.why: The notes define equivalent fractions as two or more fractions having the same value but different numerators and denominators.

mcqs.q: Umar coloured 1/2 of his strip and Sana coloured 2/4 of her strip. Who coloured more?
mcqs.why: Comparing the two strips shows both coloured parts are equal, because 1/2 = 2/4, so neither coloured more than the other.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 2: (1 x 2)/(2 x 2) = 2/4, so 2/4 has the same value as 1/2.

mcqs.q: Which set shows fractions that all equal 1/2?
mcqs.why: Check each value: 2/4 = 1/2, 4/8 = 1/2 and 3/6 = 1/2, so 1/2, 2/4, 4/8 and 3/6 are all equivalent.

mcqs.q: How do we write that 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent?
mcqs.why: Equivalent fractions have the same value, so we use the equals sign and write 1/2 = 2/4, as shown in the notes.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 3: (1 x 3)/(2 x 3) = 3/6, so 3/6 has the same value as 1/2.

mcqs.q: Which statement about 2/3 and 1/2 is true?
mcqs.why: The fraction 2/4 simplifies to 1/2, but 2/3 does not: 2/3 is greater than 1/2, so 2/3 is not equivalent to 1/2.

mcqs.q: What makes 1/2 and 4/8 equivalent fractions?
mcqs.why: Divide 4/8 top and bottom by 4 to get 1/2. They look different but have the same value, which makes them equivalent.

mcqs.q: Sana divided her strip into 4 parts and coloured 2 parts. What fraction did she colour?
mcqs.why: Coloured parts go on top and total parts below: 2 coloured parts out of 4 parts in total gives the fraction 2/4.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 4: (1 x 4)/(2 x 4) = 4/8, so 4/8 has the same value as 1/2.

lessons.notes_html: Two or more fractions having the same value but different numerators and denominators are called equivalent fractions. Now we will identify the equivalent fractions from the given figures. Umar divided his strip into 2 equal parts. He colored one part or 1/2. His sister Sana divided her strip into 4 parts. She coloured 2 parts or 2/4. Who coloured more? When you compare the two strips, you will see that both parts are equal. We say, the two fractions are equivalent. Mathematically, we write it as: 1/2 = 2/4. Hence, these fractions are known as equivalent fractions. Example (page 91): Use fraction bars to show other fractions that equal 1/2. Solution: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 = 3/6. Equivalent fractions are two or more fractions that have the same value.

lessons.title: Families of Equivalent Fractions (page 92)

mcqs.q: How is a family of equivalent fractions made?
options: By adding the same number to top and bottom
By multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number
mcqs.why: The notes say a family is generated by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number, keeping the value the same.

mcqs.q: Which fraction belongs to the family of 1/3?
mcqs.why: Multiply 1/3 top and bottom by 2: (1 x 2)/(3 x 2) = 2/6, so 2/6 belongs to the family of 1/3.

mcqs.q: What is (1 x 4)/(3 x 4) in the family of 1/3?
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator of 1/3 by 4: numerator 1 x 4 = 4 and denominator 3 x 4 = 12, giving 4/12.

mcqs.q: Which set is the family of 1/3?
mcqs.why: Multiply 1/3 by 2, 3 and 4 top and bottom: 2/6, 3/9 and 4/12, so the family is 1/3, 2/6, 3/9 and 4/12.

mcqs.q: Which fraction belongs to the family of 3/5?
mcqs.why: Multiply 3/5 top and bottom by 2: (3 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 6/10, so 6/10 belongs to the family of 3/5.

mcqs.q: What is (3 x 3)/(5 x 3) in the family of 3/5?
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator of 3/5 by 3: numerator 3 x 3 = 9 and denominator 5 x 3 = 15, giving 9/15.

mcqs.q: Which set is the family of 3/5?
mcqs.why: Multiply 3/5 by 2, 3 and 4 top and bottom: 6/10, 9/15 and 12/20, so the family is 3/5, 6/10, 9/15 and 12/20.

mcqs.q: Write three equivalent fractions for 2/5.
Write three equivalent fractions for 3/4.
Which family does 8/10 belong to, from the exercise for 4/5?
mcqs.why: Multiply 4/5 top and bottom by 2: (4 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 8/10, so 8/10 is in the family of 4/5 with 12/15 and 16/20.

lessons.notes_html:
A family of equivalent fractions usually means a set or a group generated by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number. For example: Family of 1/3: (1 x 2)/(3 x 2) = 2/6; (1 x 3)/(3 x 3) = 3/9; (1 x 4)/(3 x 4) = 4/12. Thus, 1/3, 2/6, 3/9 and 4/12 are all parts of the same family of equivalent fractions of 1/3. Family of 3/5: (3 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 6/10; (3 x 3)/(5 x 3) = 9/15; (3 x 4)/(5 x 4) = 12/20. So, 3/5, 6/10, 9/15 and 12/20 are all parts of another family of equivalent fractions of 3/5. Teacher note (page 92): equivalent fractions are individual fractions that have the same value, such as 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 = 3/6. Families of equivalent fractions: a group of equivalent fractions to one specific original fraction such as 3/5, 6/10, 9/15, 12/20, etc. You can say that: 2/4 is an equivalent fraction of 1/2; 2/4, 3/6 and 4/8 are the family of equivalent fractions.

lessons.title: Simplifying Fractions to its Lowest Form (page 95)

mcqs.q: How do we simplify a fraction to its lowest form?
options: Add the same number to top and bottom
Divide numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number
Subtract the denominator from the numerator
mcqs.why: The notes say dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number reduces the fraction to its lowest form.

mcqs.q: Simplify 16/24 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide by 2 three times: 16/24 = 8/12, then 8/12 = 4/6, then 4/6 = 2/3, so the lowest form of 16/24 is 2/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify 28/36 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 4: 28 divided by 4 is 7 and 36 divided by 4 is 9, giving 7/9.

mcqs.q: Simplify 36/27 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 9: 36 divided by 9 is 4 and 27 divided by 9 is 3, giving 4/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify 40/70 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 10: 40 divided by 10 is 4 and 70 divided by 10 is 7, giving 4/7.

mcqs.q: Simplify 21/42 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 21: 21 divided by 21 is 1 and 42 divided by 21 is 2, giving 1/2.

mcqs.q: Simplify 66/99 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 33: 66 divided by 33 is 2 and 99 divided by 33 is 3, giving 2/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify 84/140 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 28: 84 divided by 28 is 3 and 140 divided by 28 is 5, giving 3/5.

mcqs.q: Simplify 52/80 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 4: 52 divided by 4 is 13 and 80 divided by 4 is 20, giving 13/20.

mcqs.q: Simplify 90/240 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide numerator and denominator by the common divisor 30: 90 divided by 30 is 3 and 240 divided by 30 is 8, giving 3/8.

lessons.notes_html:
If a fraction's numerator and denominator are divided by the same non-zero number, it reduces the fraction to its lowest form. Example (page 95): Simplify fraction 16/24 to its lowest form. Solution: Step-I: Divide the numerator and denominator of the fraction 16/24 by the common divisor 2: (16 / 2)/(24 / 2) = 8/12. Step-II: Divide the numerator and denominator of the fraction 8/12 by 2 again: (8 / 2)/(12 / 2) = 4/6. Step-III: Divide the numerator and denominator of the fraction 4/6 by 2 again: (4 / 2)/(6 / 2) = 2/3. So, 2/3 is the simplified or the lowest form of the fraction 16/24.
